text: A block of mass 2 kg moving on a horizontal surface with speed of $4 ms^{-1}$ enters a rough surface ranging from x = 0.5 m to x = 1.5 m. The retarding force in this range of rough surface is related to distance by F = $-$kx where $k = 12 Nm^{-1}$. The speed of the block as it just crosses the rough surface will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The initial kinetic energy of the block is $K_{i}=\dfrac{1}{2}(2)(4)^{2}=16\text{J}$.

Work done by the retarding force $F=-12x$ between $x=0.5\text{m}$ and $x=1.5\text{m}$:

$W=-12\int\limits _{0.5}^{1.5}xdx=-12\left [\dfrac{(1.5)^{2}-(0.5)^{2}}{2}\right ]=-12\text{J}$

By the work-energy theorem, $K_{f}=K_{i}+W=16-12=4\text{J}$, so

$\dfrac{1}{2}(2)v^{2}=4\Rightarrow v=2.0\text{m s}^{-1}$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Evening Shift

text:
A coil is placed in a time varying magnetic field. If the number of turns in the coil were to be halved and the radius of wire doubled, the electrical power dissipated due to the current induced in the coil would be :

(Assume the coil to be short circuited.)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The electrical power dissipated due to the current induced in a coil placed in a time-varying magnetic field can be determined by considering Faraday's Law of Induction and the resistance of the coil.

Faraday's Law of Induction
The induced EMF ($\mathcal{E}$) in a coil with $N$ turns experiencing a time-varying magnetic flux ($\Phi _{B}$) is given by:

$\mathcal{E}=-N\frac{d\Phi _{B}}{dt}$

Resistance of the Coil
The resistance ($R$) of a wire depends on its length ($L$) and cross-sectional area ($A$) as well as the resistivity ($ρ$) of the material:

$R=\frac{ρL}{A}$

For a coil of radius $r$ and with wire of radius $a$, assuming the wire is wound tightly with a length approximated by the circumference of the coil multiplied by the number of turns, we have:

$L\approx 2πrN$

And the cross-sectional area of the wire is given by:

$A=πa^{2}$

Thus, the resistance becomes:

$R\approx \frac{ρ\cdot 2πrN}{πa^{2}}=\frac{2ρrN}{a^{2}}$

Power Dissipated
The electrical power ($P$) dissipated in the coil is related to the induced current ($I$) and the resistance ($R$):

$P=I^{2}R$

Using Ohm's Law, the induced current $I$ can be expressed as:

$I=\frac{\mathcal{E}}{R}$

Substituting the expressions for $\mathcal{E}$ and $R$:

$I=\frac{N\frac{d\Phi B}{dt}}{\frac{2ρrN}{a2}}=\frac{a^{2}}{2ρr}\cdot \frac{d\Phi _{B}}{dt}$

Hence, the power dissipated:

$P=\left (\frac{a^{2}}{2ρr}\cdot \frac{d\Phi _{B}}{dt}\right )^{2}\cdot \frac{2ρrN}{a^{2}}$

$P=\frac{a^{4}}{4ρ^{2}r^{2}}\left (\frac{d\Phi _{B}}{dt}\right )^{2}\cdot \frac{2ρrN}{a^{2}}$

$P=\frac{a^{2}}{2ρr}\cdot N\left (\frac{d\Phi _{B}}{dt}\right )^{2}$

Case when the number of turns is halved and the radius of the wire is doubled
Halving the number of turns:

$N^{'}=\frac{N}{2}$

Doubling the radius of the wire:

$a^{'}=2a$

Substituting these into the power formula:

$P^{'}=\frac{(2a)^{2}}{2ρr}\cdot \frac{N}{2}\left (\frac{d\Phi _{B}}{dt}\right )^{2}$

$P^{'}=\frac{4a^{2}}{2ρr}\cdot \frac{N}{2}\left (\frac{d\Phi _{B}}{dt}\right )^{2}$

$P^{'}=\frac{4a^{2}}{2ρr}\cdot \frac{N}{2}\left (\frac{d\Phi _{B}}{dt}\right )^{2}$

$P^{'}=2\left (\frac{a^{2}}{2ρr}\cdot N\left (\frac{d\Phi _{B}}{dt}\right )^{2}\right )$

$P^{'}=2P$

Thus, the electrical power dissipated in the coil would be:

Option D

Doubled

text:
A zener of breakdown voltage $V_{z} = 8 V$ and maximum zener current, $I_{ZM} = 10 mA$ is subjected to an input voltage $V_{i} = 10 V$ with series resistance R = 100 $\Omega$. In the given circuit $R_{L}$ represents the variable load resistance. The ratio of maximum and minimum value of $R_{L}$ is $_____________$.

 
[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The Zener diode is reverse biased (cathode towards the positive rail) and regulates only while it is in breakdown, with $V_{Z}=8\text{V}$ across $R_{L}$ and a Zener current between $0$ and $I_{ZM}=10\text{mA}$.

Minimum $R_{L}$: the Zener just reaches breakdown with zero Zener current, so $R$ and $R_{L}$ form a simple divider giving $8\text{V}$ across $R_{L}$:

$\dfrac{R_{L}}{R_{L}+100}\times 10=8\Rightarrow R_{L}=400\Omega$

For a smaller $R_{L}$ the voltage across it is below $8\text{V}$ and the Zener does not conduct.

Maximum $R_{L}$: in breakdown the current through $R$ is fixed at

$I_{R}=\dfrac{10-8}{100}=20\text{mA}$

The Zener current $I_{R}-I_{L}$ must not exceed $10\text{mA}$, so $I_{L}\geq 10\text{mA}$:

$\dfrac{8}{R_{L}}\geq 10\times 10^{-3}\Rightarrow R_{L}\leq 800\Omega$

$\dfrac{R_{L,\max }}{R_{L,\min }}=\dfrac{800}{400}=2$

Hence, the answer is 2.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Evening Shift

text: A liquid of density 750 kgm$^{-3}$ flows smoothly through a horizontal pipe that tapers in cross-sectional area from $A_{1} = 1.2$ $\times$ $10^{-2} m^{2}$ to $A_{2} =$ $\frac{A_{1}}{2}$. $P_{1}+\frac{1}{2}ρv^{2}=P_{2}+\frac{1}{2}ρ4v^{2}$
